title: Muhammad Suraj Salihu
text:
About Me



Muhammad Suraj Salihu


Alhamdulillah for my first (test) Quarto website.

My Progress
This website is also my learning journal.
Rather than treating the course as something that ends after twelve or so weeks, I want to use this space to document what I learn, the projects I work on, the problems I encounter, and how my skills develop over time.
I will be adding new projects, notes, analyses, and reflections as I continue learning.
This is the beginning of my journey into bioinformatics.
On this date 30th August 2026
Thank you Dr Popoola. Thank you CBR. Cheers!

title: About
text:
I am a medical student at Bayero University Kano with a growing interest in bioinformatics, computational biology, and data-driven medicine.
My interest in bioinformatics comes from wanting to understand how computational approaches can complement clinical medicine and biomedical research. As a medical student, I have seen how much biological and clinical information is generated every day, and I am interested in learning how programming and computational methods can be used to make sense of this information.


I joined the Applied Bioinformatics for Beginners course at the Centre for Biotechnology Research (CBR), Bayero University Kano, because I wanted to move beyond simply being interested in bioinformatics and actually develop practical skills.
I am particularly interested in learning how to work with biological sequences, analyse genomic data, use Linux and Python, and eventually apply these skills to real biomedical and public-health problems.
I am grateful to Dr. Popoola, our tutor, for guiding us through the course and introducing us to the practical side of bioinformatics.



Through this course, I hope to:

Make Mama proud
Become more comfortable using the Linux command line.
Improve my Python and data-analysis skills.
Learn how to analyse and interpret biological sequence data.
Build a portfolio that documents my progress and projects.




This website is also my learning journal.
Rather than treating the course as something that ends after eight weeks, I want to use this space to document what I learn, the projects I work on, the problems I encounter, and how my skills develop over time.
I will be adding new projects, notes, analyses, and reflections as I continue learning.
This is the beginning of my journey into bioinformatics.
